newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices rally late on technical strength.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices rally late on technical strength.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices staged an afternoon rally Wednesday for the second consecutive session as crude's technical strength eclipsed shipment problems and bullish inventory data as the market's fuel upwards.
At 1452 EST, April crude was up 39 cents at $22.45.

"What's going on is the funds are (buy) stopping out of crude. All other stories are mere excuses for gains at this point," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products at Paribas Futures Inc in New York. Dealers noted spot crude has broken key resistance levels in the last two sessions, triggering buy stops used by traders to cover short poistions.
April gasoline was up 0.72 cent at 68.00 cents a gallon while April heating oil was up 0.07 cent a gallon at 56.25 cents.

Refined product shipments were being detained by the closure of the Mississippi River, but dealers were quick to point out that only about 10 to 15 percent of refined product from the U.S. Gulf refineries are shipped on the river.
Moreover, those shipments are primarily for the Midcontinent, and not the New York Harbor which the NYMEX gasoline contract reflects.
The Mississippi River was closed late Monday following a barge accident north of Baton Rouge, Lousiana.

Spot crude had broken trendline resistance on the April chart that lay around $20.50 and that extends from the April contract high of $25.30 on January 9. The same level also reprsented 50 percent retracement from the contract high to April's seven month low of $19.86.
